review.summary: The manuscript is a faithful, complete and very readable presentation of the archived zt-neutral run (props P1–P9; plan simplest@claude-opus-5-5). I re-derived every proposition. Theorem 1.1 (i)–(iii) matches archived P9 exactly in hypotheses, error terms, the range x^{7/9+δ} ≤ f(y) ≤ x^{1−δ}, η = min(δ/12, 1/(6d)) and the uniformity. The weight f'(k) and the class of f are unchanged. Every local correction listed in changes.md is mathematically correct, and each is either authorised by the operator audit, raised by the run's referees, or an expository fix. I checked them individually: P1(iii) normalisation and convergence, the P3 constant 14→7, the P8 endpoint via Lemma 8.5 on arbitrary intervals, and the 449/8 total in P5(b). The reformulation of the Euler–Maclaurin b=∞ clause (Lemma 2.6) keeps the archived hypotheses, is true, and leaves both applications unchanged. It is not a source gap. The numerics come from an unchanged re-run of the accepted snapshot code with matching hashes. My independent checks agree with the archived results and the shipped tables: brute-force V_f on 6 rows, Euler products for C_f computed with my own code, the symbolic Vaughan local identity, and an independent check of the exact identity. Citations check against the supplied PDFs. Provenance matches provenance.json and interventions.md, and there is no claim of human authorship. The PDF (32 pages, no overfull boxes, no undefined references) renders cleanly. Three minor fixes remain: (1) the abstract omits the standing hypothesis y ≥ 1, without which its stated asymptotic is literally false; (2) changes.md says the round-3 feedback files are 'in this workspace', but they are not in the supplied package; (3) Remark 1.2 uses an undefined δ in one threshold sentence. None of these affects the mathematics.
issues: Abstract (main.tex, abstract): the statement 'for each fixed δ∈(0,1/9), V_f(x,y)=C_f x^{1/2}f(y)^{3/2}(1+O(x^{-η})) uniformly for x^{7/9+δ}≤f(y)≤x^{1−δ}' does not state y≥1. Read on its own it is false: for f=t^2+1 and y=−x^{0.45}, f(y) lies in the range but V_f(x,y)=0 because the k-sum is empty. In the body this is covered by the convention after (1.2) ('y≥1 is real') and by the quantifier of Theorem 1.1, which mirrors archived P9. Fix: add 'real y≥1' to the abstract. Optionally repeat 'x≥2, y≥1' in Theorem 1.1(iii).

manuscript/changes.md, 'Feedback files' paragraph (and §4 item 19, §9): the text says the round-3 review files 'feedback/0.json' and 'feedback/1.json' are 'in this workspace'. No feedback/ directory exists in the supplied package, so the round-4 responses in §9 cannot be checked against those files. Fix: either include the files or say they were in the writer's workspace and are not part of this package, as is already done for rounds 1–2.

Remark 1.2 (sections/01-introduction.tex): 'It is smaller than x^{1/2}Y^{3/2} only when Y ≥ x^{7/9+δ}' uses δ before it is defined in this context, and the threshold is imprecise. x^{5/3+ε} < x^{1/2}Y^{3/2} holds exactly when Y > x^{7/9+2ε/3}. Suggest 'only when Y is larger than x^{7/9+2ε/3}, i.e. essentially Y > x^{7/9}'. Cosmetic.

For Markus's attention, not blocking: Lemma 2.6 states the infinite-interval Euler–Maclaurin clause of the archived P5 proof precisely: the limit of partial-sum minus partial-integral exists, and the series converges iff the integral does. The archived hypotheses are kept. I checked that this is true and that both applications have absolutely convergent series and integrals. changes.md §10 correctly lists it as awaiting Markus's acknowledgement. No mathematical change and no source gap.
review.statement_checks:
I compared each manuscript statement with the archived statement.md files and re-derived the proofs.
- Thm 1.1(i),(ii),(iii) match P9 verbatim: x≥2, y≥1, Y=f(y)≤x; errors x^{1/3+ε}Y^{5/3}+x^{5/3+ε}+x^{1/2+ε}Y^{3/2−1/(2d)} and x^{5/3+ε}+x^{1/2}Y; δ∈(0,1/9), η=min(δ/12,1/(6d)), constants O_{f,δ}. Positivity of C_f comes from P8(0). The definitions of σ_p (=τ_p), C_f=(2/3)I∏σ_p, h(q), MT, A_0, η and m_t are identical to the archived ones up to the renaming documented in changes.md §2.
- Prop 3.1 = P1(i)–(v). (iii) is stated for n∈N, and the archived misnormalisation (extra factor q) and the false bound Σ|h(p)|≤Σp^{-2} are corrected. I confirmed q=n=2 gives |u(2)|=1/2.
- Lemma 3.2 and Prop 3.3 = P4, with c_0=3e^{2ζ(3/2)} taken from the P4 proof.
- Prop 4.1 = P2 exactly. Prop 5.1 = P3. The constant (3+9C(ε)) uses the correct (2π²/3z)Σ1/e ≤ 7τ(m)/z; I verified the arithmetic.
- Prop 6.1 = P5(a)–(c) with c_1=60. I re-checked the integration by parts in (a), the five Euler–Maclaurin remainders R_1..R_5 and the total 449/8 Λ<57Λ, the convolution β=μ*κ_q, and Σβ(n)/n=Δ_q.
- Prop 6.2 = P6, stated for all x>0 and q∈N. This broader range is exactly what the archived proof records (P6 Step 2, 'No use was made of q≤x or x≥1'), and changes.md §4a lists it.
- Prop 7.1 = P7. Prop 8.1 = P8(0),(a)–(c) for all real y≥1. I checked Lemma 8.2's identities (also symbolically), ρ(p²)≤pρ(p), the convex-combination positivity of σ_p, |σ_p−1|≤(3+2d)/p², the bounds (8.5)–(8.7), the truncation bound, and the assembly with ε≤1/8.
- Section 9: the composition of constants and the three ratio estimates in (iii) are correct. The added Remark 9.1 (sharper exponents −17δ/12 and −5/(18d)) is correct and keeps the archived η.
- Remark 6.3, added material: b_p/a_p≥1−1/p and c_p/a_p=(p+1)/(p+2) hold, so h(q)≥IA_hφ(q)/q. The x→0 counterexample for q>x is correct.
- Only flaw found: the abstract drops y≥1 (see issues).
review.dependency_checks:
I checked every use of a proposition against its contract.
- Prop 7.1 uses Prop 4.1 (all x≥1, q∈N), Prop 5.1 (x≥2, 1≤m=hq≤x; holds since h≤x/q), Prop 3.3 (x≥1, q≤x) and Prop 6.2 (any x>0, q).
- Section 9 uses Prop 7.1 for q=f(k) with 2≤f(k)≤Y≤x; f is increasing because f'≥1 on real t≥1, and this is now explicit in (1.1). It uses Prop 8.1(a)–(c) for real y≥1, and (9.2) y^{-1/2}≤γ_0^{1/(2d)}Y^{-1/(2d)}.
- The ε-splitting (ε/2 in (ii), ε/3 in (i)) composes correctly into c(f,ε). x≥2 is used only for P3, as the remark states.
- Prop 6.2 needs Prop 6.1(c) for every Z_1>0, which (c) provides. Prop 6.1(c) needs (b) for every real Z>0, which (b) provides, including Z<1.
- Prop 8.1(a)'s Euler product (8.8) uses absolute convergence from (8.6). Lemma 8.5 is applied on ≤2d−1 disjoint intervals built from the closed monotonicity intervals of Lemma 8.4. This removes the archived (1−δ,β] device that needed F left of 1, as flagged by the Opus P8 reviewer for f=3t−1.
- Lemma 2.5 is merged from P1(iv) and P3 Step 4; the regrouping by n=ab with G(n)=μ(n)2^{ω(n)}n^{-2}1[(n,e)=1] is valid by Theorem 1.9 of Montgomery–Vaughan 2007.
- Lemma 2.6: under the archived hypotheses the limit formula holds, and both applications (u^{-s} with Re s>1; Φ=Z/u²−Z²/u⁴) have absolutely convergent series and integrals, so P5 is unaffected.
- The archived referee objections (P1 Sol and Opus, P3 Opus, P8 Opus and Sol) match the attributions in changes.md §4.
- I found no interface mismatch and no use of a result outside its stated range.
review.numerics_checks:
Computation path:
- reproduce.py checks the SHA-256 of compute.py and counts.cpp against accepted.json (I confirmed 0f8d7bc6… for compute.py), copies them unchanged, recompiles counts.cpp with clang++ -O3 and re-runs the full grid. reproduce.log shows all 11 sizes plus the two diagnostic re-runs and an exact comparison: integer counts identical, max relative difference of V = 0, identical fits.
- I compared generated/snapshot_rerun_results.json with the archived results.json myself: all 270 V_decimal strings are identical.
- build-inputs.json hashes match the shipped main.pdf, macros.tex and tab_shape.tex.
- Tables 2, 3, 4 and 6–8 and Figures 1–2 are written from the re-run; they are recomputed, not copied.

Independent checks I ran:
- Brute-force V_f(x,y) at x=2.5e5 for r=0.01 and 0.1, for all three polynomials (6 rows), using direct residue counts and the closed form of g. All agree with the archived values to ≤1.6e−15 relative.
- My own Euler-product code (ρ by brute force for p<300, closed forms beyond) gives C_f partials at p≤1e6 of 0.13808266, 0.13560756 and 0.14261335, matching Table 1.
- sympy confirms σ_p(ρ≡1)=C_{1,p}(1−p^{-2})², so C_t equals Vaughan's c_2.
- An independent implementation of Prop 4.1 at x=5000 for q∈{7,12,18,49,60,97}: V−RHS = 0.0072, constant across q. This is the expected size of my own truncation of the MT tail; reproduce.py's closed-form tails reach 4.8e−10. MT−h(q)√(xq) stays within x^{1/3}q^{2/3}.

Code review of reproduce.py:
- MT closed forms (A_0Σ_{(t,q)=1}η = (6/π²)∏(p²−2)/(p²−1), and the analogous η/t² sum) are correct.
- The identity self-test uses the general g formula, valid for all l.
- The tail bound (8·K/(1−K/N²))(N^{-2}+1/(30N)) is valid, since P_0=∅ for the three polynomials.
- The ρ formulas for k³+2 (cubic-residue test) and k²+1 are correct and are also brute-forced for p<1000.
- Bounds are rounded outwards and checked by the script. I spot-checked the macros against reproduction.json: δ_row, the shape interval [0.9938, 1.0011], β in [1.538, 1.552], N ranges, stability 0.91% and 0.04%, x^{-1/3}r^{-3/2}≈1.6, and δ_row,max≈0.103 at r=0.1.
- The extrapolations (−2.61%, +0.53%, −0.65%; all within the heuristic envelopes) agree with the integrators' figures in interventions.md.

Limitations:
- I did not re-run the full 11-minute, 5 GB snapshot myself. I relied on its log, the hash checks and my brute-force spot checks.
- Floating-point rounding in the C_f partial products is checked but not certified, as the text itself states.
review.citation_checks:
Checked against the supplied PDFs.
- Vaughan 2005: the Theorem (1.12)–(1.13), c_k (1.14) and C_1 (1.15) specialise at k=2 to (1.3) exactly. The error terms x^{1/4}Y^{7/4}exp(…) and x^{3/2}exp(…), the 'x sufficiently large' convention, Q_1 in (1.16), the earlier results (1.6)–(1.11), and the reliance on BGPVW ('The core of the proof depends heavily on [1]') all match. The DOI matches the PDF header.
- Brüdern–Wooley: the §1 Theorem (degree ≥2, weight f'(k), f(y)≤x) and the attribution of the method to Goldston–Vaughan [3] and Vaughan [10] (= Vaughan 1998 I) match. The reference list confirms GV 1997 (LMS LNS 237, 117–142) and Vaughan 1998 I (PTRSA 356, 781–791). The PDF is a 2009 preprint; the venue Quart. J. Math. 62 (2011) 289–305 comes from papers/INDEX.md, as the README says.
- BGPVW §1 (PDF p. 3): reports Evelyn–Linfoot's elementary error O(n^{2/(k+1)+ε}) for the binary k-free problem, as quoted in Section 5. Volume and pages come from INDEX.md, since the PDF has no journal header.
- Montgomery–Vaughan 2007: (2.20) d(n)≤C(ε)n^ε, Theorem 1.8 (product of absolutely convergent Dirichlet series), Theorem 1.9 (Euler product for multiplicative f), Theorem 1.12 (continuation via {u}) and Corollary 10.4 (functional equation) were all verified in the supplied chapters. Theorem B.5 is correctly not cited, since Appendix B is not in the corpus.
- The DOIs for GV 1997, Vaughan 1998 I and MV 2007 match INDEX.md. No locator is invented for BGPVW or BW; the bibliography notes say so.
- All six cited works are in the supplied corpus. The only post-2010 item is BW 2011, as allowed.
- Not verifiable from the supplied material: the Evelyn–Linfoot, Orr, Warlimont and Croft originals. These are correctly mentioned only as quoted by BGPVW and Vaughan and are not cited separately.
- The Mirsky citation from earlier drafts has been removed.
- Excluded material: none of the excluded author's work and not the excluded Dehnert paper appears among the cited or consulted sources. I did not search for, open or use either.
review.provenance_checks:
Appendix B and changes.md were checked against provenance.json and source/interventions.md.
- Records match: repository URL with archive label zt-neutral, archive commit ed0aebaf…, harness commit 33aadc60…, revision 8dfc53d0…; model roles (planner and probe Opus/Sol plus Sonnet probe; numerics Sonnet/Sol with the Sol snapshot accepted; prover Sonnet; referees Opus and Sol; integrators Opus and Sol); CLI versions 2.1.309 and codex-cli 0.166.0; write-up stage claude-opus-5-5 under 2.1.311 with reviewers Opus and Sol. The text says CLI versions are not model-weight versions.
- The account of events matches interventions.md: plan selection by Markus, all P1–P9 passing in round 1, the integrators' composition finding, Markus's quoted decision, the operator audit and its three listed corrections, and the independent checks (Sol direct counts of the 16 rows at x=250000; Opus Σf'MT comparison).
- The title-page byline reads 'Write-up of an archived machine-generated proof run'. There is no claim of human authorship.
- Archived work is clearly separated from later corrections, which are grouped (a) audit, (b) run referees, (c) write-up stage.
- Compliance notes are kept in Appendix B, README and changes.md §6, out of the mathematical exposition.
- Exposure: the repository URL belongs to the excluded author's GitLab namespace. It is only stated for reproducibility, as allowed. I did not browse it, and nothing in the manuscript draws on it.
- Inaccuracy: changes.md says the round-3 feedback files are 'in this workspace', but they are not in the supplied package (see issues). I could not check the claimed round-1 to round-3 write-up review history; changes.md itself says those summaries are the writer's own.
review.layout_checks:
- I extracted the whole PDF with pdftotext -layout and rendered all 32 pages at 80 dpi with pdftoppm. I inspected pages 1, 3, 4, 6, 8, 13, 15, 20, 21 and 24–32 visually, covering the title, abstract and table of contents, the theorem, Lemmas 2.4–2.6, Prop 3.1, the sawtooth proof, Section 8.3, Section 9, all numerics tables and figures, the references, Appendix A and Appendix B. pdftotext shows no '??'.
- main.log has no overfull or underfull boxes and no undefined references or citations; the only warning is the harmless epstopdf shell-escape notice.
- Equations are well typeset and legible. Long displays (Vaughan's formula, (8.8), the assembly display of 8.3, the Euler–Maclaurin remainders) fit the text width, and equation numbering is per section.
- Tables 1–8 are readable; Table 3 headers are fractions with an explanatory caption. Figures 1–3 render correctly, with legends, axis labels and C_f markers at r=0. The Figure 3 caption explains the shared legend. The FloatBarrier keeps floats out of §10.5.
- The bibliography (plainurl) is complete for the six cited works, with notes on missing locators.
- Notation is consistent with the declared conventions (σ_p, a_p/b_p/c_p, Δ_q, κ_q, h♮, w, γ_i), and there is no clash with E, B or A(m).
- Only textual nit: the threshold sentence in Remark 1.2 (see issues).
- I did not recompile the PDF; build.log and build-inputs.json hashes match the shipped main.pdf.
